solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very successful but cheesy play?

parts.note: Agatha Christie's whodunnit has run in London since 1952, and the device for catching rodents is baited with cheese

explanation.surface: A critic sums up a hit show that is also corny and sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheesy' looks like an insult to the play's quality, but it points to the cheese used as bait in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Christie's thriller is the longest-running stage play in the world, so it is famously successful.

clue.text: Schoolmasters' discussion? Not action-packed programmes?

definitions.meaning: head teachers chatting among themselves, taking the phrase literally
television shows that consist of people speaking to camera, with little happening

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'heads' as headmasters; the second is the TV term for shows built around a speaker filmed from the shoulders up.
explanation.definitionFit: Television jargon names static monologue shows after the speaker's face filling the frame, and head teachers conversing would literally match.

clue.text: Deeply impress rampaging avenger

indicators.note: rampaging means rushing about wildly, so the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A furious avenger on the loose leaves a lasting impression on everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave something on the mind is to fix it there firmly, a figurative sense of cutting into a surface.

clue.text: No change in gland

parts.note: no as a number is nil, shown as the letter O
to change is to vary

explanation.surface: A medical report says a gland shows no alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovaries are the female reproductive organs that also secrete hormones, so they count as glands.

clue.text: Extremely sore martial artist finds chair

indicators.note: extremely is read as at the extremes, so only the outermost letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: a dan is a graded expert in judo or karate

explanation.surface: A judo black belt, aching all over, gratefully sinks into a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles, so the shorter word names that kind of chair.

clue.text: I'd train to change long-established belief

indicators.note: change asks for the letters of the words just given to be altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone says they will train themselves out of an old, ingrained conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom or belief handed down through generations is what tradition means.

clue.text: Cap may be impossible to understand

definitions.meaning: a cap sits on top of the skull, so literally it is positioned higher than the wearer's crown
the idiom for something too difficult for a person to grasp

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally, where a hat sits; the second is the idiom for being beyond someone's comprehension.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea that is too clever for you is said to go over you, beyond your grasp; a cap literally rests on the crown.

clue.text: Humble request: the hopeless don't have one

definitions.meaning: an appeal made meekly, as to God
the idiom saying a no-hoper has no chance at all

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading turns on the phrase 'not have a ...', meaning to stand no chance whatever.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplication is a humble plea, and someone with no chance of success is said not to have one.

clue.text: Pull girl over who is dawdling

indicators.note: over signals turning the whole string of letters round so it reads from the end

parts.note: to pull is to drag
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone tells a slow companion to haul a girl across to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DRAGGAL round from end to start.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word describes someone slow and lagging behind, just as dawdling does.

clue.text: Almost grieve after a love affair

indicators.note: after places the shortened word behind the single letter
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to grieve is to mourn

explanation.surface: Someone is close to grieving once a romance is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from MOURN to leave MOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word is used in English for a romance, often a secret one.

clue.text: Land in hospital — yuk!

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies concealed inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A patient complains about the food in a hospital somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The country in southern Europe is a land, a simple general-to-specific example.

clue.text: Awful vanity punctured by English simplicity

indicators.note: punctured by means pierced, so the abbreviation goes into the middle of the scrambled letters
awful suggests the letters of the following word are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: Dreadful conceit is deflated by plain English honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges VANITY into NAIVTY, and 'punctured by' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent simplicity and lack of worldliness is what the word describes.

clue.text: Shine, putting energy into a sort of rock

indicators.note: putting one thing into another means the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: glam rock is a flamboyant 1970s style of rock music
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Polishing a stone with vigour makes it glint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests a stone, but it is music.
explanation.definitionFit: A glimmer of light is a gleam, and as a verb it means to give out a soft shine.

clue.text: One day, looked at becoming rich

parts.note: Monday, one of the days of the week, is abbreviated Mon
to have looked at something is to have eyed it

explanation.surface: One day someone was ogled after striking it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a numeral, but it belongs with 'day' as one particular day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Having plenty of money means being wealthy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Less powerful, the river surrounds pub

indicators.note: the letters before this word go round the word after it

parts.note: taken as written
an inn is a pub
R is the usual map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A weakening river flows round a riverside pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A diluted drink or a weaker argument is less strong, the comparative sense of thin.

clue.text: Musical interval: tenor struggles with it

indicators.note: struggles suggests the letters are wrestled about into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer finds a tricky interval hard to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval of three whole tones, an augmented fourth, is a famously awkward one in music.

clue.text: Once strain, creating annexe?

parts.note: ex means former, what something once was
strain is tension

explanation.surface: Building work on a new wing causes stress for the household.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an example of an addition built onto a house, hence the question mark.

clue.text: In France, you stick up for royal house

parts.note: tu is the French familiar word for you

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A French speaker urges a friend to defend the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ROD to DOR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The dynasty of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I ruled England from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Small bill is miserable

parts.note: a bill is a poster, an advertisement, shortened to ad

explanation.surface: A small invoice leaves someone feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling unhappy or wretched is a direct synonym of feeling low.

clue.text: Girl, nervous but attractive

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
shy means timid or nervous

explanation.surface: A young woman is timid yet good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for good-looking, especially of a man, often said of a heartthrob.

clue.text: Flier old man's given to fielders

indicators.note: given to means added on to, joining the two pieces

parts.note: old man is slang for father, daddy; the 's is read as 'is'
long leg is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side, so fielders there are long legs

explanation.surface: Dad has been handed a team of cricket fielders.
explanation.walkthrough: LONG LEG is a cricket fielding position deep behind the batter on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly, with its gangly limbs, is an insect, and anything that flies is a flier.

clue.text: Obtained travel ticket at last

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: at last picks out only the final letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A traveller finally managed to buy a ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of get, which means acquired or came to possess.

clue.text: Game Irish saint can't finish

indicators.note: unable to finish means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: St Bridget, also Brigid, is a patron saint of Ireland

explanation.surface: A holy woman from Ireland cannot complete her game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't finish' drops the T from BRIDGET.
explanation.definitionFit: The trick-taking card game for two partnerships is played socially and in tournaments.

clue.text: Prosecutor breaks plaything now

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the first piece goes into the middle of the second

parts.note: a toy is a plaything
DA is a District Attorney, an American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A lawyer smashes a child's toy in the present.
explanation.definitionFit: The present day or nowadays, the adverb meaning at this time.
